script: What's the medical condition that keeps making Musiala collapse? So, Jamal Musiala is one of the brightest young stars in world football, a twenty-three-year-old who plays for Bayern Munich and is a key man for Germany. During a pre-season friendly against RB Leipzig, he suddenly collapsed on the pitch, and because it was hot that day, over thirty degrees Celsius, a lot of people just assumed the heat was getting to him. But the heat theory fell apart four days later at a different game where the weather wasn't the story at all. In another friendly against Heidenheim, Musiala came on as a substitute, and just minutes after stepping onto the field, he went down again. Players from both teams rushed over and formed a circle around him while the medical staff treated him, and even though he looked dazed, a staff member had to help him walk off the pitch. This made it two collapses in four days from a healthy young athlete, and nobody watching knew why. But Musiala himself was the one who finally ended the guessing, and what he revealed wasn't a muscle or a bone at all. He revealed that doctors had diagnosed him with something called absence seizures, which is a type of epileptic seizure that causes a brief, sudden lapse in awareness, usually lasting only a few seconds. A person basically stares blankly and stops what they're doing before snapping back to normal, which is why Musiala looked so out of it before recovering quickly. He says the condition is easily treatable and that there's no further health risk to his overall health, so that's why he's continuing to play football for the time being.
